steps.title: Ethics in sport
steps.body: The moral principles and values that govern behaviour in sport. Ethics determine what is considered right and wrong, fair and unfair, and guide the conduct of performers, coaches, officials and spectators.

steps.title: Etiquette
steps.body: The unwritten rules, conventions and customs that govern behaviour in sport. Etiquette is about showing respect, courtesy and consideration for others. It is not enforced by officials but is expected by the sporting community.

steps.title: Etiquette vs Rules
steps.body: Etiquette is NOT the same as the written rules of the sport. Rules are formally codified and enforced by officials with penalties for breaches. Etiquette is unwritten, self-policed and based on respect and tradition. Breaking etiquette has no formal punishment but damages a performer's reputation.

steps.title: Sportsmanship
steps.body: Behaviour that shows fairness, respect and generosity towards opponents. A sportsmanlike player plays within the spirit of the sport, not just the letter of the rules. Sportsmanship goes beyond what is required and reflects positive moral character.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the clear definitions of all four terms - examiners test these directly Etiquette = unwritten conventions; Sportsmanship = fair play beyond rules; Gamesmanship = bending rules; Contract = agreement to compete fairly Always give named sporting examples for each concept Gamesmanship is NOT cheating - it stays within the letter of the rules The contract to compete is about mutual agreement - if one party breaks it, the competition is unfair Be prepared to evaluate whether a specific behaviour is gamesmanship or cheating
